body:
I don't consider this a breaking change. The previous behaviour was broken and the code in question added an error message to explain that the code was broken. 

In general bug fixes are not considered breaking changes since doing so would flood the migration doc. However, some bug fixes are considered breaking changes, especially if they change the behaviour of features that were working previous to the bug fix. 

This PR adds a guard across behaviour that is invalid. If anyone hits the error its because their code is buggy and needs to be fixed. In that way the error is a sort of self-documenting mechanism. You don't need to be notified that the error may occur. It automatically gets printed for any user that needs to see if. 

Therefore, I wouldn't document this change as a breaking change.

@clayjohn seriously?

From 4.6.3
> The Z axis of the from_pos, to_pos and size must be 0 for 2-dimensional textures.

In 4.7
> For 2-dimensional textures, from_pos and to_pos must have a Z axis of 0, and size must have a Z axis of 1.

The API changed in a breaking way. Please add this to https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html because it is 100% a change that must be made when migrating code that followed the API of 4.6.3.

> This page intends to cover everything you need to pay attention to when migrating your project.
> If you are migrating from 4.6 to 4.7, the breaking changes listed here might affect you.

You are just wrong about this being a "bug fix," this was the documented requirement and code ran perfectly well before this change. This has affected a PR I have open right now, which I was quick to test and update, but it was annoying to find no information about this and have to check the doc and git blame to see. What was the bug that this fixed? The commit only modified the documentation and added the lines that fail the function call, so it really looks like an arbitrary change. I'm sure there was a reason, but whatever it was, it wasn't part of that commit. If the change log is ordered, I didn't notice a surrounding change that looked related.

> What was the bug that this fixed?

See the original PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118239

The code running perfectly was luck. The configurations you had just happened to work correctly.

The PR:
> The issue is, some drivers seem to not care about zero values on Vulkan and copy anyway

You agree that:
> The code running perfectly was luck. The configurations you had just happened to work correctly.

And clay also agrees that:
> However, some bug fixes are considered breaking changes, especially if they change the behaviour of features that were working previous to the bug fix

So let me get it straight, this is not a logical bug, as it worked on some Vulkan drivers, but an API "bug," which needed only a change to the API and introduces an error message. Why does this not fit the criteria of a breaking API change that should be mentioned in the migration guide?

I must be taking crazy pills because I'm being told that a change to the API which breaks previously working code does not fit the definition of a breaking API change, and also is not fit to be mentioned in the migration guide? Copying a texture is not even an obscure thing, it might even be the most common thing to do with a texture for post processing shaders.

Looking more closely at the guide, most of the Rendering section is mentioning new optional parameters, and a renamed parameter. None of these could cause existing code to stop working. How are those fitting the criteria while this does not? Again, I must be taking crazy pills.
